textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 5 evs · Journey of a River · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: The Godavari begins near Nashik in Maharashtra. It is called Dakshina Ganga because it flows through southern India and is regarded as sacred.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: The Godavari begins near Nashik in Maharashtra. It is called Dakshina Ganga because it flows through southern India and is regarded as sacred.
beats.speakEn: The Godavari begins near Nashik in Maharashtra. It is called Dakshina Ganga because it flows through southern India and is regarded as sacred.

beats.en: Streams that join a river are its tributaries. Some tributaries receive water only in the rainy season, so they are seasonal rivers.
beats.speakEn: Streams that join a river are its tributaries. Some tributaries receive water only in the rainy season, so they are seasonal rivers.

textbookBox.concept: The river flows through rich forests with tigers, barking deer, the Indian golden gecko and red sandalwood trees.

beats.en: The river flows through rich forests with tigers, barking deer, the Indian golden gecko and red sandalwood trees.

beats.en: When the river reaches the sea, it spreads out into many small streams that form a delta. Its freshwater meets the salty sea at the Coringa Mangrove Forests, where the journey ends.
